name: Chainsaw, electric or battery

comps.spec: DC motor, 36–80 V (cordless models; brushless or brushed: check the motor's label)
36–80V tool battery packs (cordless models; often taken with the saw)
comps.loc: Battery slot or charger on the shelf

notes: Salvage: a corded saw gives a mains motor and its cord (2,400 W on the 230 V Oregon CS1500); a battery saw gives a motor and the battery pack, 36 V on STIHL's AK saws and 80 V on the Greenworks Pro (Oregon CS1500, STIHL MSA 60/70, Greenworks Pro 80V). The saws checked carry the same kind of bar, chain, drive sprocket and oil tank as a petrol saw and can kick back (Oregon CS1500, Greenworks Pro 80V, Oregon M&S 2004); chaps may not stop them as surely, because the motor keeps its torque (UW Extension chainsaw). Quieter than petrol but not quiet: sound pressure levels of 83 dB(A) on the STIHL MSA 60 and 96 dB(A) on the Oregon CS1500, and all three makers call for hearing protection (STIHL MSA 60/70, Oregon CS1500, Greenworks Pro 80V). STIHL recommends charging its packs at 5–40 °C, so warm a cold pack indoors before charging it, and warns that one charged or used below −20 °C or above +50 °C may catch fire or explode (STIHL MSA 60/70).
